subject.title: [Feature]: sessions_kill should terminate all child exec processes spawned by a session

question: What public session exec-control contract and authorization boundary should OpenClaw expose for listing and terminating child exec processes spawned by a stored session?
rationale: The missing behavior is source-proven, but exposing process visibility and termination by session can cross agent/session/sandbox boundaries and needs an owner-approved product and security model before implementation.

options.title: Add guarded session exec control
options.body: Add new Gateway and CLI methods for session exec list and kill with explicit operator scope, canonical session resolution, per-run outcomes, and tests for child, PTY, sandbox, and fallback behavior.

options.title: Extend existing abort/delete explicitly
options.body: Add opt-in kill-exec flags to existing session maintenance methods while preserving current defaults and documenting upgrade behavior.

options.title: Defer public process control
options.body: Keep the existing agent-scoped process tool only and track orphan/restart cleanup in narrower lifecycle issues until a broader process-control design is ready.

recommendation.title: Add guarded session exec control
recommendation.body: Add new Gateway and CLI methods for session exec list and kill with explicit operator scope, canonical session resolution, per-run outcomes, and tests for child, PTY, sandbox, and fallback behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent is already connected to this issue timeline and has recent gateway security/session-boundary history.
